# Extension matrix fixtures (task-111)

Small, deterministic, committed inputs for the extension matrix harness
(`scripts/ext-matrix.mjs`, task-110). The harness loads an input with
`loadInput(id, inputDir?)` from `scripts/lib/ext-matrix-outputs.mjs`, invokes the
real tool, and judges the result with `validateToolOutput(id, result)`.

## Layout

- `inputs/*.json` — one committed argument object per matrix invocation. They
  contain NO machine paths: asset references are relative (`./assets/...`) and
  `loadInput` rewrites them to absolute paths (or, for `image.describe`'s typed
  media input, reads the bytes into `{ mediaType, bytes }`).
- `assets/` — generated by `build-fixtures.mjs`
  (`node packages/dsh-model-as-tool/tests/fixtures/ext-matrix/build-fixtures.mjs`).
  The fixture test re-runs the builders and asserts the committed bytes are
  byte-for-byte identical, so these files cannot drift.
- Extra inputs not in `MATRIX_TOOLS` (`lang-detect-fr/de/ja/zh/ambiguous.json`,
  `stt-transcribe-silence.json`) exist for the offline validator tests. They
  validate against the same declared schemas.

## What each asset can and cannot prove

**`assets/tone-2s-16k-mono.wav`** — a deterministic 2.0 s synthesized tone:
180 Hz fundamental plus harmonics, 4 Hz amplitude modulation, 16 kHz mono
16-bit PCM. It proves the audio path opens a valid RIFF/WAVE file, decodes the
declared sample rate, and returns the contract SHAPE with coverage bounded by
the real duration. It **cannot** prove word accuracy, language detection,
punctuation or speaker behaviour — it is not speech, and no test in this
repository claims otherwise.

**`assets/silence-1s-16k-mono.wav`** — 1.0 s of digital silence. This is the
honest empty-input case used OFFLINE: a correct transcript of silence is empty,
so the validator test asserts that `text: ""` with `transcribedSeconds: 0` is
accepted and invented words are refused. It is not invoked by the live matrix.

**`assets/tiny-canvas.png`** — a 96x64 RGB PNG with a red rectangle (8,12 to
38,42) and a blue filled circle (centre 68,32, radius 17) on a white field. It
proves `image.describe` receives real image bytes and that its description talks
about visible content rather than echoing a filename. It cannot prove exact OCR
(the image deliberately contains no text) or that any hidden detail was seen.

## Size

Total assets are under 100 KB (well below the 2 MB budget), and every fixture is
committed.
